title: dsh-conflict-doctor audit report
description: The JSON contract of one conflict audit. Callers parse this with `format: "json"`; the markdown report is a rendering of the same data. Fields are additive-only within a major version: a consumer may ignore unknown properties, but an existing property will not change meaning without a major bump.

schemaVersion.description: Version of THIS contract. Incremented on any breaking change; additive changes do not bump it.

profilePath.description: Profile directory that was read, or `(running profile)` for a live-only audit.

liveEntries.description: Loader rows examined (0 for a profile-only audit).

patchLayers.description: Patch layers examined (0 for a live-only audit).

findings.description: Every diagnosed conflict, ordered by severity then code then first ref, so the output is stable across runs.

notes.description: Non-fatal coverage gaps and the reason any check was withheld. A consumer must not read an empty finding list as 'all clear' when these explain otherwise.

versionAuthority.description: Whether the version baseline describes the RUNNING host.

kind.description: `patch` = paste into cordis.patch.yml; `command` = run in the profile; `manual` = a decision only the user can make.

risk.description: How much this repair changes, COMPUTED by the audit from `kind` and `snippet` rather than hand-labelled. `safe` adds rows and leaves existing ones alone; `caution` replaces an existing row's config, recoverable from a backup; `destructive` disables or deletes a row, or runs a command, changing what actually loads. Only `patch` fixes graded `safe` or `caution` may be applied without an explicit opt-in.

plan.description: Structured repair plan for programmatic application. Present when kind is `patch`. The snippet remains for human consumption; the plan is the authority for `--apply` and `--dry-run`.

refs.description: Entry ids, row ids, packages, or tool names this finding is about.

impact.description: What actually breaks, in user terms.

evidence.description: The facts that prove the finding. Never a guess; a finding whose evidence cannot be reproduced should be treated as unproven.

fixes.description: At least one repair. A critical finding with no actionable repair is a bug in this tool.
